subject: STR Laws and Enforcement
comment: Dear Council Members and City Officials, My name is Sean Lodge and I am a property owner on the boundary of District 3. My property sits on the border with D3, D1, & D2. I am writing to you today to better understand the City Council's recent direction regarding the regulation and enforcement of short-term rentals (STRs) within our community. It is my understanding that the City of Salt Lake has recently hired 3 full-time enforcement officers to regulate and shut down STR's within the city. As a property owner, I have been following the discussions and laws surrounding housing availability and neighborhood character. However, I am concerned about the potential economic impact of a broad shutdown of properties operating as STR's. As the Mayor continues to allow the construction high-density apartment complexes all over the City, many of which are not close to capacity and are lowering their monthly rent to increase occupancy, while stating there's a "housing crisis". I would appreciate your perspective on the following and how you will support the owners and residents within your districts: 1. Rationale for Current Restrictions What are the primary data points or community concerns driving the decision to continue the ban and shutting down short-term rentals at this time? Specifically, I am additionally interested in HB256 which allows municipalities to use online listings as primary evidence of illegal rentals, provided they have additional supporting information (like neighbor complaints). With the enforcement issuing shutdown notices they are not gathering additional information other than online platforms when I approached an enforcement officer with the question. Municipalities surrounding Salt Lake City allow STR's with proper licensing and compliance. What is the reason that Salt Lake City has decided to ban them and make them illegal? 2. Hotel Options, construction companies jobless building the apartment complexes (which there is rumor that our current Mayor's husband is involved with), or lack of understanding and ability to license and collect tourism tax's? 3. Your Personal Position on STRs Do you support a total ban, or are you in favor of a "middle ground" approach—such as a permitting system like long term rentals and allowing STR's with the ability to collect the taxes? I am eager to know if you believe there is a path forward that allows responsible owners to continue operating while mitigating the concerns of other residents and neighbors? Will the City make issue a temporary lift on the law when the 2024 Olympics come back to Utah? 3. Promoting Local Tourism Short-term rentals often attract a demographic of travelers who support our local small businesses, coffee shops, and hidden gems that are far from the traditional hotel districts. How does the Council plan to maintain or grow our local tourism economy if the available lodging options are significantly reduced? The City/State has pushed a lot of large conventions that are typically held in the downtown area away which is also pulling money and tourism out of the City and State. I believe that a vibrant city requires a balance between protecting its residents, the owners, and remaining a welcoming destination for visitors. I look forward to hearing your thoughts on how we can achieve that balance without stifling the economic contributions of the short-term rental market. Thank you for your time and for your service to our city. Sincerely, Sean Lodge

subject: Concerns regarding ICE facilities in SLC
comment: To Whom It May Concern, I write to urge the council to consider and pass an emergency ordinance requiring a conditional use permit for ICE facilities in SLC, giving the council and planning commission the legal basis to block the construction and use of detention facilities in SLC. As you may know, ICE detention facilities are inhumane, neglecting to feed, medicate, or otherwise care for those they detain. (https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/ice-stopped-paying-for-detainee-medical-care-as-population-surged/) As ICE has now begun to detain and hold children in these facilities as well, these detention centers become a massive human rights violation via the abuse and neglect of both children and adults. Additionally, these facilities allow U.S. citizens (including children) to be flown out of state, away from home or legal assistance. (https://www.cnn.com/2026/01/24/us/elvis-tipan-echeverria-toddler-ice-arrest-minnesota) The SLC City Council is responsible for protecting its constituents from such human rights abuses and danger. Thank you

subject: We've had enough
comment: I want to express something clearly: the way immigration enforcement is being handled feels like a profound misuse of resources and humanity. It's heartbreaking to watch all of this unfold and see people still willing to participate in systems that cause so much harm—just to be in someone's good graces. We should be asking ourselves whether any of this is right for anyone, regardless of documentation status. A person's birthplace shouldn't determine their worth. The color of someone's skin shouldn't determine how they're treated. None of these things make us safer, and it's frustrating to be told otherwise. With the government shutting down yet again—as if that's just normal now—it's hard not to feel disillusioned. I'm asking for a moment of humanity, a moment to recognize the damage these decisions inflict on real people and on the world around us. I'm ashamed of what this says about us as a country, and I'm ashamed that this is what being an American citizen seems to represent to some. We deserve better leadership, and we deserve people in office who value compassion, justice, and basic human dignity.

subject: Subdivision plat amendment application for 2005 South 800 East
comment: Dear Council member Young, Salt Lake City Council members, Mayor Mendenhall and members of the City Planning Commission. Please help! Please can you do something to stop this project that proposes to build 16 townhouses on the lot at 2005 S 800E next to my house. (Case number PLNSUB2025-01172) There are multiple reasons why this will harm the neighborhood. But the one most concerning to us is the horrible pollution that the construction of these units will generate if this project is allowed to go through. My husband and I have owned our house at 1997 South 800 East for 43 years. We are in our 80's and have heart and other health issues. He has heart failure and I have COPD. The dust, fumes from construction vehicles, noise and light pollution will probably kill us. I know most of our close neighbors are alarmed by this project. Some are saying they may have to move if it goes through. Please listen to us and to our neighbors and do whatever you can to stop this. Thank you. Respectfully, Ronni McDonough

subject: Re: Petition PLNSUB2025-01172
comment: Salt Lake City Planning Commission Attention: Rylee Hall I received notice last Friday that the property adjacent to my home is being targeted for the development of "16 townhouses. I am writing to strongly object to this proposal which I believe will inflict irreparable harm on this neighborhood and might result in serious health consequences for my wife and myself. My wife has COPD and both of us suffer from heart failure and respiratory issues. Dust and exhaust fumes from construction will be certain to exacerbate these conditions and might very well prove fatal. The development, if approved, is certain to increase traffic on 8th East which already suffers overflow from 7th and 9th East. Lack of adequate parking on 8th has been a growing problem for several years, and the addition of 20 or more vehicles to this end of block will inevitably force residents and visitors to park in front of our house and those of our adjoining neighbors. The plans as rendered do not provide adequate parking for the residents of the town houses, let alone any visitors. Water drainage at that specific location has been a major unresolved problem for decades. The old bed of Parley's Creek used to flow by the property but was diverted into culverts many decades ago. But water will always try to find its lowest drainage and the resulting subsidence causes street flooding yearly,. The project is out of scale for the street and would be prohibited if it were just 13 feet further north where we live and which is zoned "RESIDENTIAL" In fact, there are many aspects of this proposal which should prohibit its construction including issues of setback, height restriction etc, We have been told that the proposal is within code for that area, but the impacts affect the adjoining neighborhood where they would be prohibited. Many of these impacts will be long term and irreparable. Views of the mountains will be gone and our home will be placed in the shadow of the buildings which will block out the sun and the night sky. Long term, traffic and exhaust fumes will increase and light pollution will be exacerbated. The sustainability and liveability of the neighborhood. Whatever else happens our property values are certain to fall. I was also informed in that notice that: "Objections to this petition should be submitted no later than Feb 21st, 2026 giving me only 10 days to research and respond to the petition. During that period city n This is an . an extremely short time to research and prepare my objections. This is particularly true since city offices were open for only 4 days during the designated time allowed. I encourage you to reject this application Sincerely

subject: We need a better option
comment: Good Morning, I did a quick survey this morning of 7 people in our program. The average age was ....... 42 All had been diagnosed with a mental health condition. The average age at which they entered treatment.... 17 The avg age for when 5 of the 7 surveyed first entered treatment was ...... 12 All have been in treatment Been in Detox an average of 5.7 times Been in jail .... 12 times Born and raised in Utah .... 50% Many entered the system when they were 12-14, are now 42, and they are still living on the street. So ... either Salt Lake City will have to hire 50 more SLCPD Officers and double the size of the jail, and double the number of shelter beds to deal effectively with what is a mental health crisis...... or find better treatment programs. The least expensive option is to find programs that help the mentally ill and addicted return to becoming productive members of the community. Join us one morning, Bernie Hart Understanding Us Taylorsville, Ut

subject: A simple question
comment: Chris, I have followed up on First Step's reply to my asking for data on the effectiveness of their programs. They said the only way I could get the information was by filing a GRAMA Request with Salt Lake County. That should not be necessary. I feel that any parent or spouse should be able to ask any mental health and addiction service provider for information on the effectiveness of their program. A simple Google search, and the information should pop up. Because it does not, and is not on the internet, I assume the information does not exist. That is not acceptable. Salt Lake County does not have the information I requested on First Step. If it did, they would have given it to me without a GRAMA Request Chief Redd recently mentioned having SLCPD Social Workers become more active by referring the chronically homeless to services. Over 90% of the chronically homeless I have interviewed are dealing with mental health or addiction problems. I am assuming that SLCPD Social Workers will refer people with a drug problem to First Step or Odyssey House. As well as Valley Mental Health for mental health problems. The Salt Lake City Council approves funding for SLCPD social workers. Question: Do the SLCPD Social Workers have data on the effectiveness of the programs they refer people to? Do Chief Redd and the SLCPD Social Workers know how many people the programs have transitioned out of homelessness? Please do not tell me I have to file a GRAMA Request for information that should be at the fingertips of every elected official. Do the SLCPD programs Salt Lake City taxpayers fund work? And how well. Over 50% of the people who join us in front of the City and County Building four mornings a week entered the system before they were 14. They are now 45 and still waiting for the programs funded by Salt Lake City and County to deliver on what they promised. Simple question: Do the programs work? Bernie Hart Understanding Us Taylorsville, Ut
